public_rationale: Through April 4, Nvidia was down roughly 30%, compared with 13.7% for the S&P 500. That supports the ordinary approximate reading of 'a third' and clearly supports the market comparison. The wording slightly overstates the reported decline if read precisely.
limitations: The supported result depends on accepting approximate language: 30% is not exactly one third.
The S&P 500 is an evaluator-selected benchmark.
The Nvidia figure comes from financial reporting rather than a directly retrieved exchange price series.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Nvidia's stock fell by about a third in 2025 through early April, far more than the overall market.

statement.excerpt: NVidia is down by a third, so far in 2025. (Far more than the stock market itself.)
statement.document_title: Scaling is over, the bubble may be deflating, LLMs still can’t reason, and you can’t trust Sam

from_speaker: NVidia is down by a third

our_interpretation: Read 'a third' as an approximate description of the share-price decline, consistent with the supplied normalized proposition.
Use conventional calendar-year-to-date price performance, measured from the preceding year-end close through April 4, the last trading close before the Sunday post.
Use the S&P 500 price index as an ordinary broad US market comparator.
This is a traded-security price-return claim, rather than a claim about Nvidia's corporate finances; metric_scope is therefore null.
criteria.support_condition: Nvidia's year-to-date share-price decline is approximately one third and materially exceeds the broad market's decline over the same interval.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Nvidia's decline is materially smaller than approximately one third, or does not substantially exceed the broad market decline.
